findings.title: RDS instance without storage encryption
findings.description: RDS storage should be encrypted at rest. The provider default for storage_encrypted is false, so an absent attribute is a finding.
findings.remediation:
Enable storage encryption on the RDS instance:
resource "aws_db_instance" "this" {
  # ...
  storage_encrypted = true
  kms_key_id        = aws_kms_key.rds.arn  # optional CMK
}
Note: encryption cannot be enabled on an existing unencrypted instance —
take a snapshot, copy it with encryption, and restore.

findings.title: CloudTrail not multi-region
findings.description: A single-region trail misses API activity in every other region. is_multi_region_trail defaults to false.

evidence.actual: absent or false (provider default: single region)

findings.remediation:
Enable CloudTrail in all regions with log file validation:
resource "aws_cloudtrail" "this" {
  is_multi_region_trail         = true
  enable_log_file_validation    = true
  kms_key_id                    = aws_kms_key.cloudtrail.arn
  s3_bucket_name                = aws_s3_bucket.trail.id
  include_global_service_events = true
}

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in resource config
findings.description: A database password written as a literal in Terraform config is stored in state, plan output, and version control. The same holds for a secret-like variable or local flowing into a credential attribute. Reference a secrets manager or a generated password instead. The secret value is never included in findings.

evidence.expected: reference to a secrets manager or generated password

findings.remediation:
Remove the hardcoded credential and rotate it immediately — it is compromised.
Reference a Secrets Manager secret instead:
data "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "db" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.db.id
}
# then: password = jsondecode(data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db.secret_string)["password"]
If the value was committed to git, purge it from history (BFG/truffleHog) and rotate.

findings.title: SNS topic policy allows public principal
findings.description: The policy document contains a reference that could not be resolved statically (unresolvable jsonencode() parts), so public-principal evaluation is UNCERTAIN. Review the policy manually.

evidence.actual: UNCERTAIN: unresolvable reference unresolvable jsonencode() parts

findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

findings.title: ECR repository without KMS encryption
findings.description: ECR repositories default to AES256-managed encryption. A customer managed KMS key (encryption_type = KMS) gives key control and audit. Absent configuration defaults to AES256.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: ECR repository allows mutable image tags
findings.description: With image_tag_mutability = MUTABLE (the default when absent), an attacker who pushes to the repository can overwrite a trusted tag such as 'latest' with a malicious image. Set image_tag_mutability to IMMUTABLE so tags cannot be overwritten.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: Secrets Manager secret without customer-managed KMS key
findings.description: Secrets Manager secrets should use a customer-managed KMS key (kms_key_id) instead of the default AWS-managed key, so key rotation and access policies are under your control. Set kms_key_id.

evidence.expected: kms_key_id set to a customer-managed key

findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: IAM role has no permissions boundary
findings.description: The role sets no permissions_boundary, so nothing caps the maximum permissions its policies can grant — a single overly broad policy attachment becomes fully effective. Set a permissions boundary as a guardrail.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: RDS master password not managed by Secrets Manager
findings.description: A plaintext master password is set without manage_master_user_password, so the credential sits in state and is never rotated automatically. Use manage_master_user_password = true so RDS manages rotation in Secrets Manager. The password value is never included in findings.
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

findings.description: An aws_vpc with enable_dns_hostnames = false (the provider default) gives instances no public DNS hostnames, which breaks hostname-based service discovery and forces reliance on raw IPs. Enable DNS hostnames alongside DNS support.

findings.title: CloudTrail trail is not an organization trail
findings.description: A trail that is not an organization trail records API activity for a single account only. An organization trail centralizes audit logging across every account in the organization.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: Secrets Manager secret without description
findings.description: A secret with no description is unidentifiable in audits and secret inventories. Describe the secret's purpose and owner.
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

findings.title: SSM SecureString parameter using default KMS key
findings.description: A SecureString parameter with no key_id encrypts with the default aws/ssm key, which the account cannot rotate or scope via key policy. Point key_id at a customer-managed key.

evidence.expected: key_id set to a customer-managed KMS key

findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: Backup vault without vault lock configuration
findings.description: A Backup vault with no aws_backup_vault_lock_configuration allows recovery points to be deleted before their retention period expires, undermining ransomware protection. Add a vault lock in compliance mode with a minimum retention.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: API Gateway method without a request validator
